sources.entry: API management is the process of creating and publishing application programming interfaces (APIs), enforcing their usage policies, controlling access, nurturing the subscriber community, collecting and analyzing usage statistics, and reporting on performance.

summary.name: API management
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article describing API management, the practice of creating, publishing, securing, monitoring and monetizing web APIs, and the components typically found in API management products.
use_cases: choosing components for an api program
planning api gateway and throttling policies
setting up a developer portal for api users
charging for access to commercial apis
summary.what_it_does: This is a general encyclopedia article, not a software tool. It defines API management as creating and publishing web APIs, enforcing usage policies, controlling access, building a developer community, and analyzing usage statistics. It describes typical components: a gateway that handles throttling, security and transformation; publishing tools for API definition (OpenAPI, RAML), documentation and testing; a developer portal or API store; reporting and analytics; and monetization. It also gives market size estimates from Gartner, Forrester and KBV Research.
notable: Breaks API management into gateway, publishing tools, developer portal, analytics and monetization components
Names gateway technologies such as Nginx and HAProxy
Includes market size figures from Gartner, Forrester and KBV Research
caveats: The article itself says it needs more citations (last flagged January 2019)
Market figures are dated projections from older analyst reports
